findings.reason: merge.js:32 now returns collection.constructor(iters[0]) unconditionally. For Record({})(), RecordType without `new` calls `new RecordType(values)` (Record.js:56-57), which returns a fresh instance, so __tests__/issues.ts:135 `expect(emptyRecord.merge({ id: 1 })).toBe(emptyRecord)` fails. acceptance.md locks the baseline tests and gives no numbered criterion, so breaks is left out. C2's point that no criterion asks for this revert is the same defect seen as a scope problem.
findings.claim: Removing the isRecord guard means merging into an empty Record builds a new instance instead of returning the same one, which reintroduces Issue #1785 and fails a locked baseline test.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `import { isRecord }` and replaces `return isRecord(collection) ? collection : collection.constructor(iters[0]);` with `return collection.constructor(iters[0]);`. For `Record({})()`, `toSeq().size === 0`, so this branch runs and calls `new RecordType(values)`, which builds a fresh instance (Record.js:52-97). The unknown keys are dropped because `this._indices[k]` is undefined. `__tests__/issues.ts:133-135` asserts `expect(emptyRecord.merge({ id: 1 })).toBe(emptyRecord)`, and this code no longer returns the same reference.

findings.reason: merge.js:32 calls collection.constructor(...) without `new`. For `class X extends Record({})`, the constructor is the ES class itself, and calling a class without `new` throws. The removed isRecord guard used to return early for any Record, and subclassing Records is a supported pattern (__tests__/Record.ts:172, RecordJS.js:35).
findings.claim: For an ES-class subclass of an empty Record, merge() with a non-empty source calls the class constructor without `new` and throws a TypeError.
findings.evidence: The removed isRecord guard previously returned the unchanged empty Record. The replacement calls collection.constructor(iters[0]) without new. Record supports subclassing (as demonstrated in __tests__/Record.ts); an instance of class Empty extends Record({}) reaches this branch for merge({ x: 1 }), and invoking its class constructor as a function throws TypeError.
